name: HI-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean (D+12 partisan baseline)
Tokuda's dominant fundraising edge (~$986K raised, ~$487K on hand vs. ~$131K and ~$9K for Awa)
Incumbent Tokuda running for re-election with no outside spending against her
Prediction markets price Democratic win at roughly 97%
model.rationale: The district's D+12 lean, Tokuda's incumbency, and her roughly seven-to-one fundraising advantage over Brenton Awa all point to a comfortable Democratic hold, and markets price the race near 97% Democratic. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast rests on these fundamentals, which show no sign of a competitive race.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Awa within single digits, or a surge of outside spending against Tokuda, would be the first sign this race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Hawaii's second district is solidly Democratic, and incumbent Jill Tokuda is seeking re-election with the advantages that status brings. She has raised roughly $986,000 and holds about $487,000 in cash, while Republican Brenton Awa has raised about $131,000 with under $10,000 remaining. No outside groups are spending against Tokuda, and prediction markets give the Democratic side roughly a 97% chance of holding the seat.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, the incumbent's financial edge, and market pricing. All three point the same direction: a Democratic hold by a wide margin. The main uncertainty is simply the absence of direct polling, which keeps confidence moderate despite the lopsided fundamentals.
